posts.title: How to add life to your walls?
posts.author: Evolve
posts.intro: Give a room a focal point with colour, pattern, texture or a considered feature wall.
sections: A wall with personality
The original article explores feature walls as a way to introduce a point of interest into your home. A single surface can change the character of a room.
Explore pattern and texture
Murals and wallpaper bring graphic detail. Marble cladding, brick panels and wood-plastic-composite finishes offer different ways to introduce texture and depth.
Bring in a green element
The article includes green walls among its ideas. Evolve’s product collection also includes artificial green walls; discuss which system suits the space and the level of maintenance you want.
Start with colour
Paint is another way to change the feel of a surface. Compare the options alongside your furniture, lighting and existing finishes, then speak with the showroom team about available products.

posts.title: Different types of gypsum boards
posts.author: Evolve
posts.intro: A guide to the different roles gypsum boards can play in walls, ceilings and interior layouts.
sections: A flexible foundation
Gypsum boards are used for partitions, ceilings and interior details. They can help define rooms and create features such as recessed lighting.
Choose for the conditions

Standard white boards are commonly used indoors. Other boards are designed for increased fire resistance, moisture-prone areas or exterior sheathing. The original article also mentions specialist acoustic and impact-resistant options.
The system matters

A board’s suitability depends on its application and the complete construction. Mineral wool can be incorporated into wall and ceiling systems for thermal and acoustic requirements. Ask for a specification appropriate to your project.
Finishing the surface
A completed gypsum surface can be painted or finished with materials such as wallpaper and decorative panels. Prepare and prime the surface in line with the selected finishing system.

posts.title: How to pick the perfect paint colour for your bedroom
posts.author: Evolve
posts.intro: Choose a bedroom palette around the colours that make you feel at home.
sections: Start with what feels comfortable
Think about the atmosphere you want at the end of the day. The original article suggests looking at the colours you naturally choose in your clothing as a starting point for a personal palette.
Find the right balance
A quiet shade can feel restful, while stronger colour can bring personality. Consider how much colour you want to live with, rather than choosing a shade simply because it is fashionable.
Think beyond the walls
Furniture, fabrics and finishes should work with the wall colour. Take these elements into account before settling on your scheme.
Consider the view between rooms
Rooms can have different palettes, but colours seen together should feel considered. Explore paint samples with the Evolve team to find a combination that suits your bedroom.

posts.title: Exterior sheeting: what is it and why is it used.
posts.author: Evolve
posts.intro: A closer look at exterior sheathing, where BoardeX is used, and why the wall system matters.
sections: What is exterior sheathing?
BoardeX is an exterior façade board with a moisture-resistant core and an orange glass-fibre facing. It is used as part of exterior wall construction and as a base beneath other finishes.
Where it is used

The original article describes applications beneath metal, timber and decorative cladding, in ventilated façades, wet areas, shafts, soffits and beneath ceramic tiling. The choice depends on the complete wall assembly and the intended conditions.
Moisture resistance is not waterproofing
The article explicitly distinguishes BoardeX from a waterproofing material. Moisture resistance should not be treated as a substitute for a properly specified waterproofing system.
Consider the whole wall
Insulation, framing, cladding and board selection work together. Speak with your architect and the Evolve team about the appropriate system and current technical documentation for your project.
